Thank you for the PR, could you check for me if using UNLINK would be better here? Also pipeline, not sure how well the client handles it. My main concern would be a few 100_000 redis calls in a loop. I added this btw for local debugging / panic. Internally we garbage collect (i.e. with hashes). If you're not using  it in the regular flow, bit slower might be fine

Thanks @timonv. On the loop concern: `clear` does not issue one call per key. It walks the keyspace with `SCAN ... MATCH <prefix>:* COUNT 100` and sends a single multi-key delete per scan page, so the number of round trips scales with keys / 100 (one `SCAN` plus one delete per page), not one call per key. A pipeline would only overlap those two calls per page, and since this is a debugging/reset path rather than the regular flow, I left it out to keep the change small.

I switched the delete from `DEL` to `UNLINK` (Redis >= 4.0), so large values are reclaimed in the background and the call doesn't block the server. I also addressed the two CodeRabbit findings: the configured message-history key is now never deleted (even when it ends in a UUID), and only canonical hyphenated UUID suffixes count as node keys. The regression test now covers a UUID-suffixed history key.

Not run locally: the change builds and the test compiles, but this environment has no Docker or Redis server, so the Redis integration test itself could not be executed. CI will be its first real run. This follow-up was prepared with AI assistance.
